terra.problem: Joseph being second only to Pharaoh is a fact from outside this passage, but it has no reference.
The text does not say Joseph stays close to the embalming himself.
The Egyptians mourned, but the text does not say the whole country grieved. It also does not say the mourning was cut short or planned to last longer.
Joseph sends his message to Pharaoh through Pharaoh’s court; the explanation makes it sound as if he quotes Jacob directly to Pharaoh.
Joseph’s supposed desire to put the whole plan on the table before asking is an unstated reason.
The passage does not say everybody old enough to travel went. It says the children and the flocks and herds were left in Goshen.
The text says the Canaanites saw the mourning, not that its loudness caused them to notice it.
The text says the Canaanites saw the mourning; it does not say they heard it. The claim that silence would not have drawn a comment is also unsupported.
The text does not mention songs, but that does not establish that there were none.
The explanation is flat and repeats the same point about naming the Egyptians without adding much.
The explanation repeatedly says that the brothers’ fear was not about flocks, without adding much to the answer.
The text says Joseph wept; it does not establish that he felt no anger.
The passage does not establish that there were no soldiers in the scene. It also does not establish that soldiers would be standing.
The soldiers line does not make a clear comparison: soldiers can bow, too.
Joseph asks whether he is in God’s place; the passage does not say he is refusing a judge’s seat. The claim that judges would be sitting above him is also unsupported.
Saying that leaving is not on Joseph’s mind assigns him a thought the text does not give.
Joseph names the preservation of many lives, but the passage does not say that this is the whole point of the story or that the story is not about him at all.
Joseph saw Ephraim’s descendants to the third generation; the text does not say they all grew up.
The text does not say Joseph trusted the sons of Israel to keep the oath.
